lina: Heads-up — found a weird shape/format mismatch between single vs batch calls to embeddings/rerank in the JS SDK. Happening in the sample app during onboarding. :thinking:

lina: Quick repro: singleEmbed = await client.embeddings.create({ input: 'hello' }) -> returns embedding: [0.01, 0.02, ...] (length 1536)

lina: batchEmbed = await client.embeddings.create({ input: ['a','b'] }) -> returns embeddings: [0.01, 0.02, ..., [0.01, 0.02, ...]] (one vector is nested incorrectly; shape looks like [1536, 1536] flattened into [3072] for first item?) :bug:

matt: can you paste the raw response body? is this the SDK creating an incorrect wrapper or is the API returning odd JSON?

lina: raw response below (redacted keys):
```
{
  "data": [
    { "embedding": [0.01, 0.02, ...] },
    { "embedding": [0.01, 0.02, ...] }
  ]
}
```
but the SDK's helper returns `embeddings` as `[[0.01,0.02,...], 0.01,0.02,...]` (notice missing bracket for second item) — looks like a serialization bug when batch size==2 and one element went through a different code path.

samira: interesting. I briefly saw a similar report in the sample-app PR — batching helper flattens when there's an internal single-item optimized path. Could be our internal `flattenIfSingle` optimization.

irina: also saw a flaky retry-related issue: if auth token refresh happens mid-batch, the SDK retries and concatentates responses, which can produce duplicate vectors or wrong ordering. Might be related.

matt: ok two possible root causes: 1) batching helper normalization bug (client-side) 2) retry logic replaying/merging partial results (client-side) — less likely to be server.

lina: repro steps I used:
1) checkout sample-app branch `devex/embed-onboard`
2) set REDWOOD_API_KEY=expiring-token (simulate refresh)
3) run `node example/batch.js` with parallel requests enabled
4) observe shape mismatch and sometimes duplicated entries in local DB

lina: example code (JS):
```
const inputs = ['doc1','doc2']
const res = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'open-embed-1536', input: inputs })
console.log(res.embeddings)
```

samira: thanks — assigning to @samira to follow up? :handyman: (j/k I'll take it). I'll open a quick issue and a fix branch to normalize the helper output to always be array-of-arrays and add a test for the retry+refresh flow.

matt: suggest two fixes:
- in SDK: always run a `normalizeEmbeddings(res)` that coerces server shapes to Array<Array<number>> and preserves ordering
- in SDK: make retry logic idempotent for streaming/batch responses (don't concat partial body on retry)

irina: also add a small migration note in the sample app docs to guard naive consumers who do `res.embeddings[0].length` without normalization.

ci-bot: New issue created: DEVEX-4123 "SDK embeddings: batch shape + retry duplication" by samira (link: https://tracker/redwood/DEVEX-4123) :white_check_mark:

samira: plan -> patch in JS SDK today (normalize + unit tests), patch sample-app to call helper, and maybe create a small utility `ensureVectors(res)` in devex utils. Will ping here when PR is up.

lina: thanks! also one small UX ask: can the error message be clearer when we detect shape mismatch? Right now it throws a cryptic `TypeError: x.map is not a function` inside downstream code. A dedicated `EmbeddingShapeError` with expected vs actual would help new devs during onboarding.

matt: agreed. add that to the issue.

samira: added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/678 (draft). Will include test harness and a short snippet for the README.

lina: verified local patch — normalizes fine, and sample-app onboarding flow passes. leaving here for QA to hit before merging. :thumbsup:

matt: great, thanks. if QA sees any server-side flakiness, we'll escalate, but sounds like client bug + retry edge case.

irina: posting a short note in onboarding checklist to run `npm ci && node example/batch.js` after SDK bumps.

samira: will add changelog entry under "bugfix(embeddings): normalize batch shapes, fix retry duplication".

lina: closing the loop here once PR is merged. thanks everyone! :sparkles:
